display.title: Episode 526: Rabbi Akiva, Saved by Negel Vasser (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah program without music: why we mourn Rabbi Akiva's students, a boy says the Shema, and Rabbi Akiva in prison uses his only water to wash his hands.
display.summary_long: A program for the days of Sefirah, which opens without music. Uncle Yossi explains that there is a time to be happy and a time to be sad: between Pesach and Shavuos we hold back from celebrations, new clothes and haircuts in memory of Rabbi Akiva's students, who did not show each other respect and died in a plague that ended on Lag BaOmer. We must show honor to everyone, which leads to Ahavas Yisroel and unity. After a word on how the Shema unites us, an eleven-year-old boy from Staten Island says the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Uncle Yossi then explains that water is Hashem's precious gift, with a special power of purity, which is why we wash negel vasser every morning. The story follows: Rabbi Akiva, jailed for teaching Torah, receives water after three days without drinking and uses it to wash his hands and make a brachah, and the amazed ruler frees him and makes him his advisor. A talk on Rabbi Akiva's great rule, 'love your fellow as yourself', explains that Ahavas Yisroel leads to love of Hashem. The show ends with Tehillim chapter 20 for the Rebbe's recovery and Shabbos candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Respect every Jew; Ahavas Yisroel leads to love of Hashem, and a mitzvah done with mesiras nefesh brings Hashem's blessing.
